title: Three Flavors of XSS
description: A three-column SVG infographic comparing the data flow of stored, reflected, and DOM-based cross-site scripting, with hover tooltips on every step and color coding for legitimate flow, attacker-controlled data, and the point where the script executes.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Compare the data flow of stored, reflected, and DOM-based XSS.
Identify where the payload lives in each subtype and whether the server ever sees it.
Recognize that DOM-based XSS can be invisible to server-side logging.

instructionalStrategies: Read the three columns side by side; hover each step to reveal what makes it dangerous.
Contrast where the payload persists (stored), travels (reflected), and stays client-side (DOM-based).

assessmentQuestions.question: Which XSS subtype can be invisible to server-side logs, and why?
Why does reflected XSS require the victim to take an action while stored XSS does not?
